2. Short facts are that the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.63 of 1957 in the 3rd Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge) Tangail for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. The suit was decreed. The defendant preferred Title Appeal No.395 of 1963 which was allowed and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court was reversed. The plaintiffs preferred 2nd Appeal No.1204 of 1965 before the High Court Division and the same was allowed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division after setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court decreeing the suit. The case of the plaintiffs is that the suit land bearing C.S. Plot No.490 was part of a river during the C.S. operation of 1318 B.S. and the land was recorded in the khas khatian of various landlords. The river having had silted up the landlords gave pattan of 2.50 acres of land including the suit land to the plaintiffs in Poush 1340 B.S. Since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. By amicable partition amongst the co-sharer landlords the suit land fell in the saham of Dhaka Nawab Estate and the plaintiffs subsequently got separate khatian from the Nawab of Dhaka for 2.09 acres of land. The defendants in Falgoon, 1358 B.S. cut and took away paddy grown by the plaintiffs in the suit land and the plaintiffs filed a criminal case against the defendants and thereafter, the present suit was filed. 

 6. The definite case of the plaintiff as made out in the plaint is that the suit land was part of a river during the C.S. operation of 1318 B.S. and the land was recorded in the khas khatian of various landlords. The river had silted up and the landlords gave pattan of 2.30 acres of land including the suit land to the plaintiff in Poush 1340 B.S. His further case is that by amicable partition amongst the landlords the suit land fell in the saham of Dhaka Nawab Estate and the plaintiff subsequently got separate khatian from the Nawab Estate of Dhaka for 2.09 acres of land. But on 14th Jaishtha, 1359 B.S. the defendants cut and took away Ansh paddy grown by him from the suit land. 

 7. It appears that the plaintiff in order to4\ prove the case of pattan have produced Exts.7, 7(a), 7(b) and the trial court considered these papers and came to the conclusion that these are quite sufficient to prove the plaintiff's story of pattan. The lower Appellate Court on the other hand held that the Ext.7 series do not bear the signature of anybody and no jama has been fixed in Ext.7. The court of appeal below on perusal of Exts.7(a) and 7(b) held that the Ext.7(b) is not a pattani likhan, but it'' appears to be a receipt for deposit of money through one Rajab Ali Sikder, for an area of land measuring 2.09 acres of land. The appellate court below further held that Ext 7(b) cannot be connected with either Ext.7 or Ext. 7(a) and it is not a document for settlement of land. The appellate court below further observed that neither in the plaint nor in the evidence of P.W.I it was stated as to what was the amount of rent 4- fixed for settlement of the suit land to the plaintiff. The court of appeal below further held that Exts.2 and 2(a) the two Nazar receipts and Exts.3 and 3(a), the two proposals for pattan purported to have been granted by the Dhaka Nawab Estate have been filed by the plaintiff in support of his possession. But Ext.2 relates to land bearing Dag No.490 appertaining to khas khatian No.2 of Mouza Nischnitapur and Ext. 2(a) cannot be deciphered as to which land it relates. The appellate court below further held that no other paper was produced by the plaintiff to prove his settlement of the suit land and acceptance of nazar money by the landlords. The appellate court below further held that Ext.3 does not show the khatian number to which the land proposed for settlement related. The lower appellate court also held that Ext. 3(a) was said to be the sanction accepting the settlement of the land mentioned in Ext.3 with effect from 1348 B.S. without any reference to the khatian to which the land appertained and accordingly held that these papers were mere paper transactions. The lower appellate court further found that there is great dis-similarity in the rate of rent mentioned in Ext.3 and the rate of rent in Ext.5 series and further observed that Ext.5 and 5(m) were obtained and granted after the trouble between the parties had already started. The lower appellate court accordingly concluded that these dakhilas Ext.5 series and the pattan and sanctioning of the same by Ext.3 and 3(a) are to be taken with a grain of salt. The lower appellate court also held that Exts.4, 4(a) and 4(b) were produced to show that the plaintiff was entered into the rent roll of the Dhaka Nawab Estate as tenant with respect to the suit land but a scrutiny of the papers produced from the Dhaka Nawab Estate shows that these do not relate to the suit land.
